cards.text: MOTILLI — AI UGC YAPPER 01

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: GLP-1 gut slowdown · first-person woman · exact approved Motilli script. Three consecutive target lanes cover all 27 thought beats; selected Alicia Darling source frames follow in a separate reference lane. Proposed runtime 4:34. Cut Room is the editable storyboard; DaVinci Resolve is the production editor. Target images and voice have not been generated.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: If you're backed up on a GLP-1 and eating less isn't helping, let me explain the gut slowdown nobody warned me about. Because once I understood it, everything changed.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Presenter, chest-up in a parked car; phone at eye level. She is already looking into the lens, ready to explain.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Hook — Direct, engaged; a small lean on let me explain. No greeting, bottle or opening logo.

CUT CUE: Cold open into presenter; continue the same take into Because I was dropping weight.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Presenter identity, wardrobe and room need selection.
Timing provisional; this thought may span presenter coverage and short inserts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Because I was dropping weight. Like, the shot was actually working. But I felt backed up every single day, that uncomfortable fullness that just wouldn't shift no matter what I ate or didn't eat.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Stay on the same woman. One restrained hand gesture on the shot was actually working.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Agitation / twist — Confusion and mild frustration, conversational rather than alarmed.

CUT CUE: Continue coverage; no mandatory cut at this beat boundary.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And that's the bit that messed with my head. My jeans were getting looser but I was still picking outfits around how my stomach felt. And I didn't really know how to explain that to anyone.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Two-second wardrobe insert: her hand hesitates between two tops; return to her for I did not really know how to explain that.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:

CUT CUE: Straight cut into insert on picking outfits; continuous voice; return on personal admission.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Unique wardrobe insert; same character/clothes continuity.
Timing provisional; this thought may span presenter coverage and short inserts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So let me tell you what I was actually missing because I genuinely thought losing the weight would fix it.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Presenter pauses, then returns attention to the lens. Maintain the same parked car and camera axis.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:

CUT CUE: Stay on her through the next thought; a pickup cut only if the performance needs it.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Presenter coverage.
Timing provisional; this thought may span presenter coverage and short inserts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I was just scrolling through a GLP-1 support group on Facebook looking for answers and a gastroenterologist had left a comment on someone's post and it stopped me mid-scroll.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Two-second over-shoulder phone scroll with generic text blocks; her thumb stops. No fabricated real Facebook post or named clinician.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Discovery / authority — Curious, recalling an ordinary scroll rather than announcing a breakthrough.

CUT CUE: Insert at scrolling; return as she begins He said. Keep voice uninterrupted.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Original illustrative phone insert; any legible post needs a real source.
Timing provisional; this thought may span presenter coverage and short inserts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: He said GLP-1 meds can slow down how fast your stomach empties. Like your stomach normally contracts to push food through, and when that slows down everything just backs up. Food, waste, gas. That's where the backed-up bloated feeling is actually coming from. It wasn't a weight thing at all. It was the gut slowdown.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Brief simple stomach-to-small-intestine educational view for empties/contracts, then return to her for the recognition. No rotting-food, universal obstruction or gas-explosion depiction.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
UMP — Explain in her own voice, then land the personal realization.

CUT CUE: Anatomy insert on how fast your stomach empties; straight return at It was not a weight thing.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Medical illustration and exact causal claims require review before generation.
Timing provisional; this thought may span presenter coverage and short inserts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And I thought okay, so that's why the fiber wasn't doing anything. Because fiber helps with regularity and MiraLAX moves water into the stool. Neither one actually touches the stomach emptying speed. I had completely missed that.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Distinct colon/stool-water illustration or neutral product-category props, followed by her reaction. Do not reuse the stomach view.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Prior solutions — And I thought okay is a real reaction, not a sales pivot.

CUT CUE: Insert only during the functional comparison; return at I had completely missed that.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Distinct illustration; no fake efficacy comparison graphics.
Timing provisional; this thought may span presenter coverage and short inserts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So I went back and DM'd him. I just asked what actually helps with the slowdown.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Keep her on camera; small glance down as she recalls sending the message.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:

cards.title: EMOTION

SCRIPT
cards.text: So I went back to the group and posted the question. And this woman who'd been on Ozempic for about eight months replied.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Same presenter; natural continuation of the story.

cards.title: EMOTION

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: She said she'd spent months researching this and found three specific ingredients that research showed actually addressed the gut slowdown directly. She walked me through each one.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: She introduces the other woman’s explanation with a subtle three-finger gesture if natural.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Solution search / criteria — Set up the list as useful advice, not an ingredient commercial.

CUT CUE: Hold until First; no bottle or brand yet.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Source account and research claims require substantiation.
Timing provisional; this thought may span presenter coverage and short inserts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: First was apigenin, which comes from celery juice. It's been shown in research to activate the receptors in the gut wall that trigger those contractions. The ones that actually move food forward.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Unbranded celery stalk/juice detail; small ingredient-name overlay apigenin. Return to her while she finishes the thought.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
UMS — Slow slightly for the unfamiliar name, then return to ordinary speech.

CUT CUE: Straight cut to ingredient on apigenin; no receptor activation animation.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Distinct celery asset; receptor/contraction claim remains unresolved.
Timing provisional; this thought may span presenter coverage and short inserts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Second was chlorophyllin, a plant compound. It's been studied clinically to bind the gas-producing stuff in the gut before it gets a chance to build pressure.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Separate chlorophyllin ingredient label beside a green ingredient sample on a neutral surface. Do not identify an ordinary leaf as the finished ingredient.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
UMS — Matter-of-fact second job.

CUT CUE: Cut on Second; return after the explanation. No disappearing-gas effect.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Correct ingredient form; clinical gas-binding claim remains unresolved.
Timing provisional; this thought may span presenter coverage and short inserts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Third was a soluble prebiotic fiber. But she was specific about it because the wrong type or too much can actually make the gas worse, not better.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Return to presenter for fiber. She gives a small cautionary hand gesture on the wrong type or too much.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
UMS — Useful qualification, no alarm or condemnation of fiber.

CUT CUE: Stay through the qualifier; no third repetitive ingredient macro required.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Presenter coverage; verify exact fiber/formula claim.
Timing provisional; this thought may span presenter coverage and short inserts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: But she said she'd spent months trying to put it together herself first. Celery juice powder on its own. Chlorophyll supplements. Different fiber products. She tried all of it. None of it moved the needle the same way. She said the ratios have to be right and you can't just piece them together and get the same effect.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Two-to-three-second overhead arrangement of three separate unbranded ingredient containers, then return to her while discussing the combination.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Formulation / selection — Tell it as someone else’s experiment she heard about.

CUT CUE: Brief insert on putting it together herself; continuous narration.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Unique tabletop shot; do not depict a proven superiority experiment.
Timing provisional; this thought may span presenter coverage and short inserts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And the thing was, she'd looked. She couldn't find a single company that had put all three together properly. Until she found one.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Presenter, steady eye contact. Allow a short beat after Until she found one.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:

CUT CUE: Hold her face; product enters only after this line finishes.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Exclusivity claim requires support; preserve original copy in planning.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I get through dinner without planning to undo my jeans by dessert. That backed-up pressure that used to build from just a few bites has gone. I'm not mapping out my outfit in the morning around how uncomfortable I think I'm going to feel by lunchtime.

cards.title: VISUAL

cards.title: EMOTION

CUT CUE: Sustained shot; no exact B-roll reuse.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Testimonial result dependency.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And I know the shot gets credit for the weight coming off. But the part that made me feel like myself again was getting rid of that constant uncomfortable feeling. Because you can be losing weight on a GLP-1 and still feel awful every single day. And nobody talks about that part. I'm sharing this because nobody told me either.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Presenter looks directly at the lens. Finish nobody told me either with empathy, not indignation.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Outcome / emotional payoff — This is the reason she is telling the story; let it breathe.

CUT CUE: Same coverage into availability beat; no music crescendo prescribed.
ASSET / SOURCE GAP: Narrator’s role and account must be represented accurately.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: The only thing she mentioned, and I've found this too, is they only do batches when the full formula is ready. So I've started ordering a spare bottle halfway through mine just so I'm not sitting around waiting on the next one.

cards.title: VISUAL

cards.title: EMOTION

cards.title: REFERENCE CREATIVE · SELECTED OBSERVED SHOTS  ·  Alicia Darling · source frames, not proposed Motilli assets

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: TIMING & SCRIPT
cards.text: Exact supplied H1 + body: 892 words. 205 wpm planning pace with brief pauses; 4:34 including a 3-second end hold. 27 thought beats are not 27 cuts or generation clips. Preserve the script; align final cuts and captions to recorded words.

cards.title: PRESENTER
cards.text: One woman over 50, parked-car phone selfie, eye-level camera, available window light. Keep her identity, clothing and camera axis consistent. Engaged conversation; reactions and emotional payoffs stay on her face. Character assets not generated yet.

cards.title: CAPTIONS & CUTS
cards.text: Black sentence-case sans serif on snug white boxes, chest height, 1–2 lines. Straight cuts on spoken actions/nouns; mostly 1–3-second inserts. Exact source font is unverified. Target cut positions await voice alignment.

cards.title: VISUAL VARIETY
cards.text: Give each B-roll insert a distinct composition and action. Do not reuse the same waistband, food or science shot. Competitor images appear only in the reference lane; proposed Motilli scenes remain text until actual selected assets exist.

cards.title: EDITOR & SOUND
cards.text: Edit in DaVinci Resolve. V1 presenter; V2 inserts; V3 product; subtitle track; A1 voice, A2 room tone, A3 optional music/SFX. Live MCP connection remains pending. Reference music/SFX matching awaits critical listening.

cards.title: END HOLD & QA
cards.text: 04:31–04:34: hold the final product/CTA composition for 3 seconds with no added speech. Proposed delivery: 1080×1920, 30fps, H.264/AAC, clean and captioned versions. Check exact script, voice alignment, captions, product identity, visual variety, sound and full exported playback.

cards.title: COPY DEPENDENCIES
cards.text: Preserve source copy in planning. Before production, substantiate the physician/group accounts, ingredient mechanism and clinical claims, first-person results, exclusivity, availability and guarantee. Do not manufacture clinician posts or before/after proof.

cards.title: REFERENCE SCOPE
cards.text: Alicia Darling, TrendTrack ad 1833962050620738: about 2:56, 71 retained source shots/pickups, median 2 seconds, presenter base about 54%. Nine selected source frames shown here. The separate original Facebook ad remains unavailable. Full frame audit saved with the editing plan.

cards.title: H2 · ALTERNATE OPENING
cards.text: My doctor put me on a GLP-1 and never once mentioned what it does to your gut. I had to find out from a Facebook group. Let me tell you what I learned.

cards.title: H3 · ALTERNATE OPENING
cards.text: I was two months into a GLP-1, dropping weight, and still waking up every morning feeling backed up and uncomfortable like nothing had moved. Let me tell you what I finally found out. Because nobody told me about it either.
